source.title: VECTOR: Very Deep Convolutional Autoencoders for Non‐Resonant Background Removal in Broadband Coherent Anti‐Stokes Raman Scattering
source.authors: Zheng-Wei Wang; K. O'Dwyer; Ryan Muddiman; Tomas E. Ward; Charles H. Camp; B. Hennelly

record.tranche_reason: The study tests training-related optimization and depth effects in its own convolutional autoencoder on simulated spectroscopy data, but its outcome is spectrum-reconstruction error, not training classification error on the benchmarks named in the versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported training-loss and validation MAE comparisons for VECTOR architectures with and without skip connections. Cited claims about ResNet and vanishing gradients are not rows. Dataset performance comparisons against SpecNet and the experimental glycerol result do not test the specified training-classification claim.
record.test_reason: VECTOR uses additive encoder–decoder skip connections and batch normalization for spectrum reconstruction. Its ablations measure reconstruction MAE and training MAE, rather than the classification-training behavior in V3. It reports no initialization, width, stability-threshold, or normalization ablation testing the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that paired additive skip connections improve deeper VECTOR reconstruction and accelerate training. They attribute this to alleviating vanishing-gradient optimization difficulty, but do not directly measure gradients. Performance on experimental spectra depends on the training data, which require better modeling of real backgrounds.
record.recipe_differences: Trains a convolutional autoencoder to reconstruct clean Raman spectra from simulated CARS spectra using MAE; evaluates reconstruction error rather than classification error. Uses paired encoder-decoder skip connections and SGD.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture depth and presence of skip connections change the reported reconstruction performance and training-loss trajectory. Dataset spectral complexity changes reconstruction MAE.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.3 reports comparable validation reconstruction MAE with and without skips for VECTOR-8/10/12. Without skips, performance saturates from VECTOR-14 and worsens at VECTOR-18 relative to VECTOR-14/16. Figure 5 reports faster training with skips, especially during the first 25 epochs, and consistently better training loss for VECTOR-18 with skips.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additive encoder–decoder skip connections improve reconstruction performance and accelerate MAE optimization in deeper convolutional autoencoders for simulated CARS spectra.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.1 reports that reconstruction MAE rises with peak count and peak-width range, and VECTOR outperforms SpecNet on all nine simulated datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CARS-to-Raman reconstruction accuracy depends on spectral complexity and the reconstruction architecture.

record.problems: The reported outcomes are reconstruction MAE and training loss on simulated spectroscopy data, not classification error. Training-loss comparisons are figure-only with no numerical values stated. Experimental evaluation is a single glycerol spectrum and is described as sensitive to training data; no ground-truth Raman spectrum is strictly available for a recorded CARS spectrum.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows for the listed claim versions: all reported outcomes concern spectroscopy reconstruction, not the named classification-training behaviors. Figure 4, Figure 5, Figures 6–8, and Figure 9 report reconstruction or training-loss outcomes and are not extracted as claim rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels, and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher–student problems.
Depth-dependent training classification error in plain versus identity-shortcut networks, longer-training controls, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification is inconsistent with its own finding that no listed version is tested. Its empty rows and labels are appropriate. Figures 4–5 are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries. Figure 4 measures validation MAE; its depth trend alone cannot establish degradation of training error.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.

Plain versus residual classification training on ImageNet or CIFAR-10, and the Fixup normalization comparison. The paper uses paired encoder-decoder skip connections, not identity residual shortcuts in the stated benchmark setting.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation measures, tanh networks, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional classification networks.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness, and squared-loss training dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons for classification accuracy and learning-rate tolerance on MNIST, CIFAR-10, or ImageNet.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
